label: NETGEAR JGS516PE
description: 16-port gigabit smart managed plus switch with 802.3af PoE on ports 1-8 sharing an 85 W budget.

poe.note: JGS516PE/JGS524PE installation guide, Specifications: "Ports | JGS516PE: 16, of which ports 1-8 are PoE ports" and "Power budget | JGS516PE: 15.4W per port for ports 1-8 Maximum power budget for the switch: 85W"; "Power consumption | JGS516PE: 110W maximum with PoE". The Gigabit Ethernet Plus Switches data sheet agrees on both: the JGS516PE row is "16" copper ports, "8" "PoE 802.3af Ports", "85W" - and the 123 W on the same page is the JGS524PE's maximum power consumption, which is where the 123 W budget claim came from.

notes: Vendor figures from NETGEAR's Gigabit Ethernet Plus Switches data sheet and the JGS516PE/JGS524PE installation guide: **16 gigabit copper ports, of which ports 1-8 are 802.3af PoE ports (15.4 W per port) and ports 9-16 carry no power**, with a **total PoE budget of 85 W** - 8 x 15.4 W = 123.2 W of port ceiling against 85 W, so the budget is the limit. The 123 W figure that appears on some listings is this switch's maximum power consumption with PoE (110 W here, 123 W for the 24-port JGS524PE), not a PoE budget.
